title: Eagles bring back wide receiver on the practice squad
description: More WR depth.
fullText:
In addition to the Cam Jurgens trade, the Philadelphia Eagles officially announced three transactions on Wednesday. Here's an overview:

RB Dameon Pierce was signed from the practice squad to the active roster.

C James Brockermeyer was signed to the practice squad after visiting the team on Tuesday.

WR Erik Ezukanma was signed to the practice squad.

We already touched on the Eagles calling up Pierce and the Eagles signing Brockermeyer. Those moves are now official.

The brand new information here is the Eagles bringing Ezukanma back into the fold. The 2022 fourth-round pick by the Miami Dolphins spent time on Philly's offseason roster from mid-June until late August.

Ezukanma flashed at times during training camp practices. He also logged four preseason receptions for 36 yards and a touchdown.

The Eagles currently have seven receivers on the roster: DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Darius Cooper, Makai Lemon, Britain Covey, Hollywood Brown, and Elijah Moore. Smith might miss a second straight game due to a hamstring injury while Brown could miss his third straight due to an ankle injury.

Prior to signing Ezukanma, the Eagles had one receiver on the practice squad: Xavier Gipson.

title: Cowboys have a big opportunity against the winless Buccaneers
description: Cowboys fans should very optimistic about this week’s game
fullText:
Momentum can change very quickly in the NFL. A week ago, the Dallas Cowboys were 1-2 and coming off a heartbreaking last-second defeat in Brazil. Now they are back at .500 after a dramatic 34-30 comeback victory over the Houston Texans, and have an opportunity to move above .500 on Thursday Night Football.

Standing in their way are the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, but we have some reasons to be positive this week.

Tampa Bay arrives at AT&T Stadium at 0-4, without its starting quarterback and without one of the best players on its defense. Meanwhile, Dak Prescott is playing some of the best football in the league, CeeDee Lamb is absolutely on fire, and Javonte Williams just scored three touchdowns.

The biggest reason for confidence remains Dak Prescott. Through four games, Prescott has thrown for 1,065 yards, eight touchdowns and only one interception while completing 70% of his passes.

He has now gone three straight games without throwing an interception. That matters with the Cowboys having scored at least 31 points in each of their last three games.

On the opposite side, Tampa Bay quarterback Baker Mayfield will not play because of a thumb injury. Instead, undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels will make only his second NFL start. Daniels completed 19 of 27 passes against Green Bay last week but managed only 148 passing yards. He also threw two interceptions and was sacked three times.

Now he has to make his second start on the road at AT&T Stadium on a short week. Dallas should make that as uncomfortable as possible.

Superstar receiver CeeDee Lamb is coming off an incredible 17-catch, 189-yard performance against Houston. He now has 498 receiving yards through four games. Making that matchup even better for Dallas is the absence of Antoine Winfield Jr, one of Tampa Bay's best defensive players. Without him in the secondary, Prescott should have opportunities to attack with Lamb, Jake Ferguson and George Pickens.

Javonte Williams is another big reason to be positive for Cowboys fans. He scored three rushing touchdowns against Houston and now has four rushing scores over the last two games. This shows that Dallas does not need Prescott throwing 45 times every week. Using Williams can help control the clock and protect the quarterback.

The Buccaneers have already allowed 16 sacks in four games. Dallas has struggled to finish pressures with sacks this season, but this is a good matchup for the pass rush to finally break through and get some momentum. If Quinnen Williams and the defensive front can make Daniels uncomfortable, mistakes should follow along with a multiple sacks.

The Cowboys are finally back at AT&T Stadium after playing in Brazil and then travelling to Houston. Dallas won its only true home game so far this season, beating Washington 37-20 in healthy fashion. That environment should be difficult for a rookie quarterback making only his second career start.

The Buccaneers are 0-4, but every one of their games have been competitive. They lost 33-27 to Cincinnati, 23-19 to Cleveland, 23-16 to Minnesota, then lost 17-14 to Green Bay. The positive here for Dallas is that Tampa Bay hasn't shown it can finish those close games, but Dallas just did.

The Cowboys were behind late in Houston, took the football with 2:15 remaining and drove down the field for the winning touchdown. One team has just proved it can finish. The other is still looking for its first win.

Tampa will be without its starting quarterback, and star defensive player, plus early practice reports have listed cornerback Benjamin Morrison and linebacker SirVocea Dennis as non-participants. Rookie linebacker Josiah Trotter was also limited with a knee injury.

For Dallas, Tyler Smith is back in practice, so things are looking up. That's a lot here that's massively positive heading into Thursday Night Football.

title: Dricus Du Plessis: Nassourdine Imavov hasn't evolved enough to beat Sean Strickland
description: Dricus Du Plessis doesn't feel good about Nassourdine Imavov's chances of avenging his loss to Sean Strickland.
fullText:
Dricus Du Plessis has broken down the projected next UFC middleweight title fight.

Champion Sean Strickland (31-7 MMA, 18-7 UFC) is expected to rematch Nassourdine Imavov (17-4 MMA, 9-2 UFC) for his first title defense. Imavov is on a five-fight winning streak since losing to Strickland in a short-notice light heavyweight bout in January 2023.

Du Plessis (24-3 MMA, 10-1 UFC) is concerned with the fact that Imavov hasn't competed since outstriking Caio Borralho at UFC Fight Night 258 last September. While he sees growth in Imavov's game, Du Plessis says not in the areas needed to beat Strickland.

"Imavov, he took a long time off," Du Plessis said on Fight Forecast. "He's been out for quite a while. Obviously deserving of the next title shot, he was on a streak. But if you look at their first fight, I just don't think there was a lot of changes in Imavov's game other than he spent time on the ground defending takedowns. He did a great job at that, but that's not going to be Strickland's game plan, and I don't see in his striking a lot of change, and I definitely don't see striking changes in Strickland's game. So, I honestly believe we're going to look at the same result as the first one. I think Strickland walks forward.

"Imavov has the style of kind of hitting and running, hitting, and running, and he does a great job at that. He doesn't get into a firefight. But Strickland, if he goes forward, that pressure is just always going to – you can't let that guy go forward. Imavov's style is very similar to (Israel) Adesanya's style, and Strickland has proven that he has the antidote to that style. Pressuring, pressuring, and his defense is so good. So, even if he goes forward, he doesn't get clipped with those shots because he keeps it safe, because he prioritizes the defense. So I honestly believe we're going to hear 'and still.'"

Former UFC middleweight champion Du Plessis beat Strickland twice in title fights before losing his belt to Khamzat Chimaev. He has since rebounded with an impressive win over former ex-UFC welterweight champ Kamaru Usman in July.

This article originally appeared on MMA Junkie: Dricus Du Plessis: Nassourdine Imavov hasn't evolved enough to beat Sean Strickland

"Malik Nabers says he's 'sore.' More sore than usual. Did as much as he could at practice. Nabers said 'we'll see' as to whether it will affect his ability to play Sunday vs. Commanders. But adds he usually gets better as the week progresses," reported Jordan Raanan of ESPN on X, formerly Twitter.

title: Joe Burrow said he likes his receiver options for Bengals-Dolphins game
description: Can the Cincinnati Bengals survive without both Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins -- at least for one week?
fullText:
Is it crazy to suggest the Cincinnati Bengals could survive without Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, if only for one week?

Chase (concussion protocol) and Higgins (neck/groin) hadn't been ruled out of the Oct. 11 game against the Miami Dolphins as of Oct. 7, but neither player practiced Wednesday. And while the Bengals pass-oriented offense relies heavily on the two players, the depth at wide receiver appears to have the team sounding reasonably well-positioned if Chase and Higgins sit this weekend.

Cincinnati has receivers that quarterback Joe Burrow has growing confidence in. That could be good enough against the winless Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium.

The group of available receivers may also include rookie Colbie Young, who returned to practice Oct. 7 after he was injured against Pittsburgh Steelers.

"We'll see how this week goes with (Young), but he looked good today, and he's a big, physical guy," Burrow said. "Same archetype as Tee. We don't really know what Sunday's going to look like yet. Could be a lot of guys that haven't had a ton of reps, and it could be guys that have had a ton of reps. We'll know more as we get closer and have some practices and have some more time for those guys to recover, but I feel confident whoever we put out there, we're gonna make it work."

Burrow's available options against the Dolphins should include Dohnte Meyers and the recently re-acquired Mitch Tinsley. Meyers and Tinsley proved key on the final drive of the Bengals' Oct. 4 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, and Burrow appeared confident leaning on them. Meyers finished with seven catches for 82 yards.

Cincinnati picked Tinsley up following the Sept. 27 loss to Pittsburgh as Andrei Iosivas and Young were both sidelined due to injuries. Receiver depth was being tested, and Tinsley immediately replenished it. His three catches for 49 yards on seven targets from Burrow against the Jaguars showed his brief time away hadn't eroded his on-field relationship with the quarterback.

Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said gaining Burrow's trust is a process that can materialize at any time. Sometimes, it happens behind the scenes. It can also happen in preseason games, where the lights are brighter.

There's no ambiguity once the trust is established, Taylor said.

"You just know. It could be offseason, training camp," Taylor said. "It used to be he had to make a quick comment to me after a route. ... Now, I just know because of some play he made. I'm sure he has had his favorites over the years of guys who aren't starters."

Subtracting Chase and Higgins from the Bengals offense fundamentally changes how the unit operates, but it's not too late to get others up to speed. Burrow painted a positive outlook on the current receiver situation, saying all the players will spend the days leading up to the Miami game focusing on what they need to be prepared.

For Chase and Higgins, what's needed is rest and recovery. For the others, it's the increased opportunities in practice that will come because Chase and Higgins are sidelined for now. The Bengals have a bye week after Miami.

"Fortunately, we're in a spot where the guys we're hoping will play Sunday have millions of reps, and (Chase and Higgins) can make sure they're getting their bodies right," Burrow said. "The guys that haven't had a ton of reps will come in and take those practice reps. So, you get those reps and practice with those guys with still the hope the other guys will play. But if not, we have those reps banked throughout the week."

This article originally appeared on Cincinnati Enquirer: Joe Burrow said he likes his receiver options for Bengals-Dolphins game

title: Rams Make History Ahead of Monday Night Showdown With Bills
description: The Rams are set to make history on October 12th, as they play their fourth prime-time game in the first five games of the season. The post Rams Make History Ahead of Monday Night Showdown With Bills appeared first on LA Sports Report.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Rams are set to make history on Monday, October 12th, as they play their fourth prime-time game in the first five games of the season, becoming the first team to do so.

The Rams started the season playing the San Francisco 49ers on a Friday in Australia, which was televised on Netflix.

In Week 2, the Rams played the New York Giants on Monday Night Football, and in Week 3, they faced the Denver Broncos on Sunday Night Football.

Week 4 was the first non-prime-time game against the Philadelphia Eagles; Now, they have a Monday Night Football game against the Buffalo Bills in Week 5.

So many marquee games have come with a difficult schedule. The Rams have already played multiple contenders this year.

The Bills are one of the best teams in the AFC, and with quarterback Josh Allen coming to Los Angeles, the LA defense will get its biggest quarterback test yet.

The Buffalo defense is struggling to stop most teams, and with the Rams offense that is finally clicking into gear, the Rams will be the favorite to win.

Matthew Stafford has not gotten going yet, throwing six touchdowns but six interceptions, along with six sacks.

Stafford is making many errors he flat-out avoided last year, and for the Rams to beat the Bills, he will need to clean up his act or risk falling behind.

The Bills offense doesn't need help scoring points, and while the Rams defense is surging, Stafford could help his other half by protecting the football.

The Rams cannot take the Bills for granted, but this is the perfect chance to seize a winning record.

title: Lions S Brian Branch on return to practice: 'I'm ready to go'
description: Detroit Lions safety Brian Branch spoke to the media after returning to practice this week, saying he was "ready to go."
fullText:
Detroit Lions safety Brian Branch looked healthy, happy and, most of all, grateful.

Branch spoke to the media after practice on Wednesday, Oct. 7, nearly 10 months after a torn Achilles ended his 2025 season. And with the Pro Bowl defensive back recovering for almost a full year, Branch took the time to express how thankful he is to be in this position.

"It's been a long time coming," he said. "[There's] nothing like being back out there, especially playing with those group of guys, just getting back in the groove of things."

Branch has had limited participation in practice this week after spending the first four weeks of the regular season on injured reserve. And though the Lions haven't specified a target date for the safety's return, there's a chance that Branch will be ready to play at home against the Green Bay Packers on Oct. 25, one week after Detroit's Week 6 bye.

But even just being at practice is an exciting step for Branch.

"I love being back out there, I love this game and you can't take this game for granted," he said.

If they didn't know this already, the Lions can't take Branch for granted, either. The Lions are last in the NFL in passing yards allowed (304.0 per game) as their injury-depleted secondary has played without Branch or All-Pro safety Kerby Joseph for the first four games of the season. And while Lions coach Dan Campbell says it will take some time for Branch to start "kicking the rust off," Branch seems confident that he can return to form sooner than many expect.

"I'm getting the rust off now in practice," he said. "When I had surgery on my toe two years ago, coming back I was kind of in my head. But this time, I don't know what transpired or what's been going on with me, but I ain't in my head. I'm ready to go."

Branch said the only hurdles to his eventual return are his conditioning and physicality, both things he can take the next couple of weeks to build up. But even though he has been pestering Campbell about his return, telling the coach he has been "starving" to play, he said he appreciates the care the Lions have taken to make sure he recovers well.

"Just want to thank them for not putting me in that position," he said. "They're looking out for me, not just for now but for the long term."

Campbell said earlier on Wednesday that the Lions have been "making sure" that Branch's recovery process has gone smoothly, as the Lions now have 21 days to either activate Branch on the active roster or keep him on the PUP list for the rest of the season.

"We've been as smart as we can be with making sure that he is physically ready to [practice]," he said. "He's been in meetings, he's able to watch walk-throughs ... so he's stayed in it mentally, but it's not the same as taking reps.

"So much of it has been, 'let's focus on the rehab, the rehabilitation, and making sure that we're all in there.' Because if we don't get that right, the rest of it doesn't matter."

Both Branch and Joseph have been eligible to return to practice this week, but Joseph remains on the sidelines while recovering from a knee injury. Branch expressed optimism that he and Joseph would be sharing a field soon, saying that they have been "fighting every day" to return from injury.

That's something Lions fans want to see, and something that Branch wants to give to the fans.

"I just can't wait to show out for them when I get back," he said. "They want to see me back, I want to be back my damn self, so I'm ready to get out there."

title: Commanders QB Jayden Daniels working to ‘embrace the brace’ in return to action
description: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels will wear a large brace to protect his elbow after dislocating in Week 2
fullText:
Jayden Daniels was presented with a hypothetical situation during his Wednesday press conference that ended with a question.

Let's say it's third-and-8, respected Athletic reporter David Aldridge said, and the first-down marker is in clear and unobstructed view.

What do you do? How hard do you charge? Is the left elbow injury now protected by a big brace going to impact what you do?

Daniels answered the question with a question.

"Sure," Alridge responded. "Let's say it is."

Daniels responded in typical JD5 fashion.

"I mean, we have to do something to win, right?"

That's the conundrum Daniels will face as he returns to action following a Week 2 elbow dislocation that was a repeat of what ended his second NFL season early.

Daniels traveled from coast to coast seeing specialists and getting medical opinions of what he should do next. He decided against surgery (during the season, at least) and to where a protective element over his elbow help prevent against another dislocation.

Daniels practiced in a limited capacity during Week 4 and was a full participant on Wednesday with the anticipation that he'll play on Sunday against the New York Giants.

He talked a ton about getting used to the brace, and his steadfast decision to play on and return quickly despite the injury.

"I went through the process and it wasn't the end of everything," Daniels told on-site reporters during his weekly press conference. "I was blessed enough to still be allowed to play this game. I'm just going to go out there and embrace it. I'm going to embrace the brace. I'm not really worried to much about it. I'm going to be the best version of myself."

The best version of Daniels is the 25-year-old playing free and having fun, with a style that's productive and super fun to watch. He believes he can do all that despite the extra hardware, considering it's his non-dominant hand.

"It's my non-throwing arm," Daniels said with a smile, "So as long as I've got the right one, I think I'll be all right."

Daniels was prudent about the fact he's not quite sure how he'll react in a game, whether he'll take it a little bit easier or whether he'll end up going full throttle in the heat of the moment.

He knows that the elbow brace is part of his playing existence now and it's something he'll have to handle.

"I'm trying to get used to it," Daniels said. "It's a part of me for the time being, so I'm getting a feel for it and find ways where it's most comfortable and where I'm able to just go play."

fullText:
The launch of a collector’s box hints at a new reality: the kinds of games I grew up with are becoming a luxury item, locked behind a forbidding spending barrier

Don’t get Pushing Buttons delivered to your inbox? 
As a parent (and partner) to a habitual collector, I do feel like an unwelcome portion of my life is occupied by an endless war against stuff. Surfaces in my home ceaselessly accumulate piles of random objects: a JoyCon wrist strap, a sticker sheet, an unidentifiable plastic piece of a toy or gizmo, an Xbox 360 controller with no batteries, cases for Switch cartridges lost down the side of the sofa … Stuff encroaches everywhere, especially in a gaming household. Much as I regret the imminent disappearance of physical games, I do not regret the extra space I have in my attic as a result of switching almost entirely to downloaded games over the last decade or so.

Speaking of the imminent disappearance of physical games: Rockstar recently announced a £350 ($400) “collector’s box” of Grand Theft Auto 6 goodies … that doesn’t include the game itself. Not even a download code. The Grand Theft Auto VI: The Goodtime State – Vice City Collection, to give it its full and unwieldy name, contains a hat, a bag, a pair of sunglasses, a figurine, a poster and more, including a mirror and a “swizzle spoon” that looks, unambigiously, like a cocaine spoon. The game retails at £70, so if you want something to play alongside all your stuff, you’re looking at an outlay of £420.

I’m not about to rag on this box of merch. People love this kind of stuff, and as a lifelong collector of Japanese gatcha and blind-box toys, I am in no position to judge how people spend their money. I have a few video game special editions that I cherish – the statue that came with my copy of The Last Guardian is still on my shelf – though I also have many more that are relegated to various cupboards. But it is unusual, however, for them to be this expensive. Usually with gaming special editions, we’re talking an extra £20-50 for a statue, or a steelbook, maybe a booklet and a keyring. 2009’s Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2’s “prestige edition” came with night vision goggles for $150. In 2015, Fallout 4’s $120 collector’s edition shipped with a plastic Pip Boy wrist unit (I had one; alas, it was flimsy and disappointing).

There have been some infamously expensive gaming special editions down the years, some of which were PR stunts (see Saints Row IV’s million-dollar pack, which included a Lamborghini and cosmetic surgery – nobody bought it). But in the 2020s high-priced video game merchandise has become more common, from a Balenciaga PlayStation tie-in line to £580 for Pokémon Lego.

What’s behind this is a troubling sense that video games as we once conceived of them – console games, played at home, perhaps on a nice 4K TV – have become a luxury item. People who can afford to spend up to £790 for a console and games are perhaps now people who can afford an extra £350 for a box of merch. Continual price-rises from Xbox and PlayStation suggest that video game companies do not seem particularly worried about pricing people out. Super-expensive merch and special editions like GTA 6’s form part of the same upward trend.

This stratification of the gaming world has been happening for years, ever since the first smartphones. The vast majority of the world’s players – about 80%, according to Newzoo – play for free, or at low cost, on mobile phones. The remaining 20% of players account for a disproportionate share of spending on the high-end gaming market on consoles and PC. With merch boxes like this, games companies are really going after that 20% for all they’ve got.

I’m saddened by the idea of gaming becoming even more of a luxury hobby. On the one hand, games in the broadest sense are more accessible than ever – you’re three taps away from playing Monopoly Go on a phone at any moment. But the kinds of games I grew up with and love to write about, games that feel like worlds rather than temporary diversions, are now increasingly locked behind a spending barrier. With the increasing scarcity of physical discs and cartridges, you can’t even reliably buy them second hand any more.

I guess there’s one advantage to the increasing cost of collector’s editions: the price has removed any lingering temptation to buy them. God knows I do not need more stuff.

Keith has been playing Silver Pines, a neo-noir detective drama with point-and-click adventure sensibilities. “As I played, I discovered countless references to 80s and 90s neo-noir culture – from Blue Velvet to Twin Peaks,” he writes in our review.

“It was a pleasure to explore every broken-down movie theatre, oily car garage and sweat-stinking interrogation room, collecting weird trinkets and working out how they’d all fit together – then exploring them again (and again) when the answers failed to show up. Silver Pines is a game to sit back and wallow in, like a private eye, kicking off his wingtip shoes and pulling that bottle of bourbon from the bottom drawer as rain trickles down the window and sodium street lights paint the walls a sickly shade of yellow.”

Available on: PC, PS5, Switch 2

 Estimated playtime: 12 hours

Award-winning UK studio Ninja Theory has reportedly begun laying off staff. The creator of Hellblade was one of the developers affected by Microsoft’s programme of lay-offs and studio closures in July, and according to Xbox COO Matt Booty two agreements to keep the studio running have failed. It is a sad end to one of the UK’s most interesting development houses.

Meanwhile, Windows Central obtained the transcript to a recent in-house meeting held for Xbox staff by Xbox CEO Asha Sharma. In it, Sharma refers to the next generation Xbox platform currently known as Project Helix as “a family of devices” rather than a single console. “There is not one device that fits all,” she stated. “We will certainly have a great console first, but we also know that many players will be on the go.” Could the ROG Xbox Ally, launched in partnership with Asus last year, have just been a beta test for a fully fledged handheld Xbox?

The news site GamesIndustry.Biz has an interesting feature on Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil movie and how it has affected the Resident Evil games. Although the film led to a modest uptick in sales, the real value of movie and TV tie-ins, according to industry analysts, is that they keep those franchises in the minds of gamers so that subsequent titles benefit from the exposure. As game development cycles continue to widen, it looks like we can expect a lot more movies and TV shows to fill in the gaps.

From Super Bowl champ to master architect: Mike Tomlin’s sprawling Minecraft city is magnificent

Gears of War: E-Day – an alien invasion shouldn’t be this boring | ★★★☆☆

A question from my friend David via email:

“I keep hearing that game publishers are avoiding the whole of November because of GTA 6 – will there really be NO choice for those of us who don’t want to shoot stuff and run people over?”

Thankfully, it’s only the big western publishers who are staying clear of the GTA 6 launch window – lots of other developers are diving in regardless. Cozy strategy game Flame, Forest and Flood (try saying that three times) is launching on the same day as GTA, offering a delightful tactical alternative, set in a hex-based woodland idyl. Staying on a rural theme, the purposefully rage-inducing “precision platformer” Trees Hate You is a woodland hiking game, where you are attacked by nature. Alternatively, Football Manager 2027 is arriving on 10 November, so instead of leading a gang of drug dealers into a bloody turf war, you could lead Plymouth Argyle into the Premier League. I’m not sure which scenario is more challenging.

fullText:
Leaders worry OpenAI is not doing due diligence to vet results and that AI models aren’t accessible to broader field of mathematicians

OpenAI has astounded mathematicians after releasing hundreds of new mathematical findings on Tuesday.

The company published over 370 mathematical results across a variety of topics such as algebra, theoretical computer science and mathematical logic, showcasing what some of its most advanced artificial intelligence models are capable of.

Last month, the company solved the Navier-Stokes equation, one of the world’s toughest mathematical problems with a $1m reward for anyone who cracked it.

The achievement prompted concerns from leaders in the field who say that frontier labs should not be testing the most advanced mathematical problems on proprietary AI models that are not accessible to the broader field of mathematicians. The Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton, New Jersey, an independent group of mathematical experts, said that it does not endorse the practice.

“It is now the case that AI can output mathematical arguments in situations without the human who prompted it being able to understand the arguments, verify them, or take responsibility for them,” a statement from the organization read. “We believe that human understanding of mathematics remains of paramount importance. How, in this new era, can we work towards a new paradigm that includes human understanding of mathematics as part of responsible scholarly output?”

To address concerns from the mathematics community, OpenAI announced it would work with the Institute for Advanced Study in order to give “mathematicians a voice in how we move forward”.

The company did not indicate, however, that it would stop testing its AI models with these advanced problems. Experts in the field say they worry OpenAI is not doing the due diligence required to vet these results.

In an interview with the New York Times, Tristan Buckmaster, a New York University mathematician who was working on the Navier-Strokes problem, said mathematicians who were prompting AI models to solve equations could be providing information that helped the model get to the result.

“There’s likely to be a bunch of results where they take someone’s work and then take it to completion,” Buckmaster said.

The advisory board has also asked that AI labs grant “equitable access” to their AI models to the global mathematics community.

“The use of proprietary internal models by AI labs to do mathematical research risks creating a two-tier system where labs outrun the rest of the field, effectively alienating the mathematical community from its own discipline,” the group wrote.

fullText:
Users reject site’s explanations after detailed instructions for writing response to post on popular forum were published

Mumsnet has denied using AI to produce content after detailed instructions to help an AI model write one of its popular “am I being unreasonable” (AIBU) posts appeared on a Mumsnet message board.

Users of the long-established forum, which is known for its frank discussions of family tensions, were vexed when the AI prompt appeared in response to a user seeking advice about a family dilemma involving a neurodivergent uncle and a sick child.

The user, called AmIAComplete, had asked for “a sanity check” from other users after an awkward social interaction with their brother’s family but was met with a prompt titled AIBU Response Schema v.1.0.

It instructed an AI to write an “interpersonal reasonableness” post and “give a clear, forum-style ruling plus brief actionable advice”. It included definitions of common Mumsnet abbreviations including AIBU, ND (neurodivergent) and DD (dear daughter).

The prompt said: “do not diagnose anyone; do not demean ND people; do not imply a sick child owes social performance” and said “prioritize compassion, boundaries, and de-escalation”.

Site users called the emergence of the prompt “really creepy”, “crazy” and “so disappointing” and it fed speculation about Mumsnet’s use of AI, with one user saying: “We might as well just go and do something else then.”

Mumsnet was founded in 2000. It faced a 19% drop in its monthly unique user numbers in 2025 to 6.1 million and the number of posts fell by 600,000. It said in its latest annual report that it was “embedding AI tools to improve productivity and enhance the user experience”.

Recent research, published in Nature, has shown that AI assistance in social media risks creating “semantic garbage” and is seen by users as less informative, “robotic” and “generic”.

Soon after the prompt emerged, Mumsnet denied that it used AI to write threads and said it had come from a tool to suggest thread titles which uses an OpenAI model. But users refused to accept this explanation and some copied the prompt into an AI and found it generated a full post.

“We are not idiots,” said one user, MrsBennetsPoorNervesAreBack. “Please can you give us a transparent explanation?”

Mumsnet then said the prompt did not come from them and suggested it had somehow transferred from AmIAComplete’s computer. Again users were unconvinced and speculated the prompt must have leaked from Mumsnet’s internal system.

Mumsnet’s founder, Justine Roberts, joined the thread and confirmed the prompt had come from its system, which sends users’ drafts to OpenAI, which is meant to suggest a title, although this time it sent a prompt for a whole reply. She said it “looks like an error on their side” and said: “We don’t use AI to write threads or replies on Mumsnet.”

This explanation also failed to appease users, who said they were being “fobbed off”.

“Why would OpenAI compel itself to do/try to do something so specific if it’s never been asked to do that before from your side?” said one. “It’s like it’s appeared in the wrong place. Rather than just sprung out of thin air.”

“I just don’t know anymore what’s real and what isn’t sometimes!” they said.

Roberts told the Guardian: “I understand why it looked like it had ‘appeared in the wrong place’. But nothing in our systems asks for, stores or uses anything like it.”

She said Mumsnet had never tested a tool that drafted posts, but it used AI for coding, advertising operations, conversational analysis and flagging potentially problematic posts to moderators.

“Mumsnet works because the people on it are real,” Roberts said. “Members trust that the advice they get comes from other parents, not a machine … This episode was a useful reminder of two things. First, these systems are less predictable than the people selling them like to suggest. Second, users are understandably highly concerned that Mumsnet remains written by humans.”

fullText:
Latest model is launching in New York to target rich US buyers – and is more than 5.2 metres long and 2 metres wide

It has no rear window, will not fit into a UK parking space and – starting at £130,000 – ($172,000) is aimed squarely at rich tech industry buyers driving the wide open roads of America.

Jaguar’s electric car, the Type 01, was launched in New York on Tuesday night and marks the culmination of a two-year rebrand that has been one of the most scrutinised in automotive history.

Bosses hope the vehicle will appeal to a younger, richer audience than the manufacturer’s previous “shrinking and ageing” customer base of “men in their 50s”, said Rawdon Glover, 58, Jaguar’s managing director.

With an ultra-long bonnet, low roof and muscular design, the Type 01 is a sharp departure from its predecessor, the F-Type. It is also double the F-Type’s starting price of about £62,000.

Buyers are likely to be rich, “urban” and “very design literate, very technology literate”, Glover said. “The person making this purchase will be choosing the car because it’s a bold choice.”

A senior JLR executive close to the Type 01 project put it more bluntly: “It’s the type of car that you park up and everybody stops and says: ‘Fucking hell, what have you just turned up in?’”

The launch comes at a critical juncture for parent company Jaguar Land Rover (JLR), which has grappled with falling sales as cheaper Chinese rivals eat into its UK market share. It is still recovering from a massive cyber-attack last year that cost the economy an estimated £1.9bn.

JLR recently announced 4,000 job cuts in an attempt to save £1.7bn over two years, citing “intense competition and ongoing geopolitical uncertainty”. The Guardian understands Jaguar employees working on the Type 01 programme were offered voluntary redundancy along with the rest of JLR’s non-manufacturing workforce.

The car will go on sale in early 2027, with the first deliveries anticipated in the second half of the year.

“It’s really important that we put Jaguar back on a more solid financial footing,” Glover said. Asked if doubling prices would be effective, he said it was better than “to toil away as we have done for the last two decades in the volume premium space”.

Range Rover also unveiled its first fully electric model in September with a starting price of £154,070 compared with £107,530 for its combustion engine predecessor.

Waning demand in China, a key market for luxury cars, has also hit Jaguar hard. Glover revealed that the Type 01 will not launch in the country for “a couple of years. We’ve decided just to hold off on that.”

However, he added that China would eventually be “an important part of the equation … it’s very difficult for any car manufacturer to exclude the single largest car market in the world”.

PB Balaji, the JLR chief executive, has said the parent company will pivot towards North America and target more sales to millionaires and billionaires to turn its fortunes around.

Glover admitted that while the Type 01’s launch was in New York, it “absolutely” could have been in Silicon Valley instead, reflecting the type of buyer Jaguar is targeting. He recently took a prototype to the offices of Nvidia, the California-based AI company, whose boss, Jensen Huang, had a ride and “loved it”.

The car has no rear window, instead using a rear-facing camera feeding a screen where a traditional mirror would be. The car produces more than 1,000 horsepower and Jaguar says it will travel up to 400 miles on a single charge.

It follows a controversial rebrand that started with an ad in late 2024 featuring stern-faced models without a car in sight. The ad prompted a backlash online and was followed by the Type 00 concept car that was unveiled in “Miami pink”, which Donald Trump described it as “woke” while Nigel Farage said Jaguar deserved to go bust.

Glover admitted the backlash “wasn’t always easy” but added: “The reality is we will need to attract a new audience.”

It is just as well: at 2 metres (6ft 5in) wide the Type 01 will hog the British country lanes frequented by Jaguar’s old customer base, while at more than 5.2 metres in length it will not fit in a standard 4.8 metre UK parking space.

“There are long cars out there on the market,” Glover argued, adding that a Land Rover Defender with a wheel on the back is longer than the Type 01, which he claimed had the “turning circle of a Fiat 500” with its all-wheel steering. “It is incredibly manoeuvrable.”

The business secretary, Jonathan Reynolds, said: “Jaguar’s new EV is a crucial step in JLR’s plans to invest over £15bn in the UK, and another big vote of confidence in our world-class automotive industry.

 “This cutting-edge new model being designed, engineered and built in Britain will support thousands of jobs across the West Midlands and North West, and builds on over £1bn of UK automotive investment secured just last month – marking another step forward in our mission to reindustrialise Britain.”

title: Tropical Storm Isaias: 1st Atlantic hurricane of season expected to hit U.S. Gulf Coast
description:
Tropical Storm Isaias formed in the Gulf on Wednesday and is expected to become the first Atlantic hurricane of the season, forecasters say.
According to the National Hurricane Center in Miami, the storm will strengthen as it moves toward the U.S. Gulf Coast later this week, becoming a hurricane by Thursday morning. It could peak as a Category 2 storm with maximum sustained winds of 110 mph by Thursday night before weakening as it approaches the coast.
fullText:
Tropical Storm Isaias formed in the Gulf on Wednesday and is expected to become the first Atlantic hurricane of the season, forecasters say.

According to the National Hurricane Center in Miami, the storm will strengthen as it moves toward the U.S. Gulf Coast later this week, becoming a hurricane by Thursday morning. It could peak as a Category 2 storm with maximum sustained winds of 110 mph by Thursday night before weakening as it approaches the coast. Isaias is expected to make landfall late on Friday or early on Saturday.

It's unclear exactly where in the Gulf Coast Isaias might make landfall. Current models show the center of the storm coming onshore anywhere from eastern Mississippi to the western tip of the Florida Panhandle. Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis declared a state of emergency for 25 counties ahead of its arrival.

"Floridians should take this time to get disaster plans in place and ensure their hurricane supply kit is stocked," DeSantis said.

Emergency management officials in Mississippi and Alabama are also urging residents to begin preparing for the storm. The University of Alabama said that it is closely monitoring Isaias, but that the Crimson Tide's home football game against Georgia in Tuscaloosa, Ala., scheduled for 7:30 p.m. ET on Saturday, will go on as scheduled.

Is the storm headed your way? Follow it in real time on the new Yahoo Weather app.

The NHC said there was "an increasing risk of dangerous wind and storm surge impacts along portions of the northern Gulf Coast," adding that floods will be possible due to heavy rainfall. Isaias is expected to produce rainfall amounts of 3 to 6 inches from far southeastern Louisiana to the Florida Panhandle. Some areas could see up to 10 inches of rain.

The Atlantic hurricane season, which runs from June to November, has not gone this late in the year without a hurricane since 1905, according to the Associated Press. A typical Atlantic hurricane season produces 14 named storms, of which seven become hurricanes. This year, there have been nine named storms, and no hurricanes.

According to the hurricane center's latest advisory, as of 5 p.m. ET on Wednesday:

Isaias was located about 500 miles southwest of the mouth of the Mississippi River

It had maximum sustained winds of 65 mph

It was moving east-northeast at 8 mph

Hurricane, tropical storm and storm surge watches have been issued across portions of the northern Gulf Coast.

A hurricane watch is in effect for:

Bay St. Louis, Miss., to Indian Pass, Fla.

A tropical storm watch is in effect for:

The Jefferson/Plaquemines Parish line in Louisiana to Bay St. Louis, Miss.

Indian Pass, Fla. to Aucilla River, Fla.

A storm surge watch is in effect for:

The mouth of the Mississippi River to Yankeetown, Fla.

A hurricane watch means that hurricane conditions are possible within the watch area, per NHC. It is typically issued 48 hours before the anticipated arrival of tropical-storm-force winds.

A tropical storm watch means that tropical storm conditions are possible within the watch area within 48 hours.

A storm surge watch means there is a possibility of "life-threatening inundation from rising water moving inland" during the next 48 hours.

An unusually strong El Niño has contributed to the relatively quiet Atlantic hurricane season by increasing wind shear — rapid changes in wind speed or direction with height — which can disrupt tropical storms and make it harder for them to strengthen into hurricanes.

fullText:
The contract for a new plant in Baltimore is the latest linked to the brothers.

President Donald Trump announced a $6.6 billion investment with AI defense company Anduril Industries on Tuesday -- the most recent government funding agreement into a company with investment ties to the president's sons.

The Trump administration announced the Navy will support $2.9 billion of the total cost to help create a new facility in Baltimore County, Maryland, that will manufacture critical parts for the Virginia-class nuclear-powered fast-attack submarine.

"In a tremendous victory for our country and for the city of Baltimore, Anduril is investing $3.7 billion in a state-of-the-art shipyard that will be known forever as Arsenal-2," Trump said at an event announcing the investment.

"Right here in Sparrows Point, you'll build the next generation of American submarines, including autonomous subs, torpedo tubes, and critical components for our cutting edge Virginia-class attack submarines," Trump said.

1789 Capital -- a venture capital firm that lists Donald Trump Jr. as one of six partners along with three founders -- claimed a stake in Anduril in June 2025 from a $2.5 billion investment into the company.

Since that investment, Anduril has been awarded 135 other contracts with the U.S. government and to date has received around $1.8 billion from those agreements, according to active defense contracts posted to SAM.gov, the official system for government contracting.

Anduril did not respond for comment on its contracts or investments from 1789 Capital, though the company has been awarded contracts dating back to 2019, according to USASpending.gov

The company is one of the largest manufacturers to receive an investment from Donald Trump Jr. and his brother Eric Trump, but they are not the only one.

An ABC News analysis found defense companies backed by the president's sons, including Anduril, have now raked in more than $6 billion dollars in active or promised government contracts since those investments were made, according to the government's official contract reporting.

This comes as Congressional Oversight Democrats continue to demand the Pentagon's inspector general investigate the approved deals.

"Refusal to investigate these serious allegations will raise significant concerns about whether your office is able to perform its statutory duty as an independent watchdog over DoD," lawmakers Richard Blumenthal, Elizabeth Warren, Robert Garcia and Tammy Duckworth wrote in a letter to Platte B. Moring, III, the Pentagon's inspector general, in May.

A Pentagon official told ABC News, "No company receives preferential treatment. The War Department always looks for solutions to benefit the warfighter, not any pre-selected entity. Outside affiliations, investors, or political connections play absolutely no role in the Department's funding decisions."

A spokesperson for the Trump brothers denied any wrongdoing.

"Don and Eric are experienced business leaders who have built and invested in businesses across a wide range of industries for decades, long before their father first ran for public office. Their investment decisions are based solely on their independent business judgment and personal convictions and they do not seek to influence, direct, or participate in any government decision, procurement, award, regulatory action, or other governmental process. Attempts to portray their ordinary investment activities as improper are a deliberate distortion of the facts," the spokesperson said.

The White House declined to comment.

Shortly after Trump won the presidency, Donald Trump Jr. was named an adviser for Florida-based drone manufacturer Unusual Machines -- a company which had not previously won any government contracts.

In October 2025, Unusual Machines scored a direct U.S. Dept. of Defense agreement for 3,500 orders of National Defense Authorization Act-compliant motors, with a potential order of 20,000 on the way in 2026.

The Trump brothers are also listed as "notable investors" for the U.S. drone company Powerus, the company announced in March 2026.

Despite not having any government contracts previously, Powerus won its first Air Force purchase order just one month later for an undisclosed amount.

In July, Powerus was awarded up to $90 million for aerial-denial unmanned aircraft systems from the U.S. Air Force.

ABC News asked Powerus if it was concerned at all about the involvement of the Trump brothers in the company, given its active contracts.

"Defense procurement is merit-based. You can't sell the government something that won't protect a soldier, and nobody in the procurement chain risks their career routing a contract to a company whose equipment doesn't work," a spokesperson for Powerus said.

"Neither Donald Trump Jr. nor Eric Trump is an advisor to Powerus, and neither is involved in the company's day-to-day business," the spokesperson continued. "Their interest is indirect, held through American Ventures, an investor in the company."

Trump-linked investments extend into the manufacturing industry, with the brothers combining for more than $1 billion across companies in mining, quantum computing and aerospace.

Oversight Democrats in their letter to the DoD criticized Donald Trump Jr.'s portfolio in raw materials, citing an August 2025 investment into Vulcan Elements, a rare-earth mining company that harvests critical materials for defense manufacturing.

That same month, the Office of Strategic Capital loaned Vulcan Elements $620 million to expand its operation.

Vulcan Elements did not respond for comment when asked about these contracts and the investments from 1789 Capital.

The firm also invested $60 million in Texas-based Firehawk Aerospace, according to firm portfolios provided by PitchBook. In the same month, Firehawk won a $4.9 million Air Force contract to "Advance Hybrid Rocket Engine Development," according to a company press release.

Firehawk would later secure tens of millions more -- $3.2 million in May 2026, an undisclosed "multimillion-dollar" contract with the Air Force Research Laboratory in July and $24 million in Dept. of Defense munitions contracts in August, according to company press releases and active contracts.

Firehawk Aerospace has been awarded government contracts across both the Biden and Trump administrations since the company's founding in 2019.

In a statement to ABC News, Firehawk said its award is "solely the product of engineering expertise and capacity."

"We value the many investors who back that mission and share our conviction that the Nation's arsenal must be built to last. Our focus is the duty in front of us, making the arsenal of the U.S. and our allies stronger," a Firehawk spokesperson said.

ABC News also found 1789 Capital raised $1 billion in revenue generation for California-based PsiQuantum in September of last year, with the company's pre-existing contract with DoD expanding by more than $157 million since then, according to SAM.gov.

PsiQuantum also signed a $100 million letter of intent with the Department of Commerce and another $125 million with the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency in May and July of 2026.

PsiQuantum did not respond when asked for comment on these investments.

Trump-linked investments were found in the automation sector.

Eric Trump said he was named chief strategy adviser for Foundation Future Industries, a humanoid robot startup with the stated aim to develop autonomous soldiers and workers.

Eric Trump touted a $24 million contract in April -- the company's first -- according to Eric Trump and CEO Sankaet Pathal's statements on Fox News. Pathal did not respond for comment on this contract or on Trump's involvement with the company's operations.

ABC News found a $391 million 1789 Capital investment into Hadrian -- a highly automated, AI-driven manufacturing company -- in the early days of 2026.

The company won its first public contracts a few months later in March -- a $39.2 million agreement with the Army for machinery and manufacturing and a $900 million deal with the Navy to create highly automated submarine factories.

Hadrian did not respond for comment when asked about these contracts.

Congressional Democrats continue to sound the alarm over these investments, referring ABC News to their May demand to the Department of Defense to launch an investigation into the president's family.

"We hope that your office will take seriously these latest concerns about corruption in the DoD award process and fulfill your statutory responsibility by initiating a review," the lawmakers wrote in their letter.
