title: 10 Hacks Every Plex User Should Know
description: Level up your media streaming capabilities with this collection of Plex tips.
fullText:
Plex has been around for almost 20 years at this point, and has added plenty of features and functions in that time. We've previously covered some of the ways it can be useful for creating your own personal streaming service.

Even if you're a seasoned Plex user, you should find something of use here, as there's everything from tweaking the metadata that the apps use to create your library, to improving the quality of your video streams—with a particular focus on films and TV shows (though Plex is capable of handling music and photos, too).

Your filenames and folder structure should give Plex enough information to correctly label TV shows and movies, but it doesn't always get it right every time. If you spot a mistake then there are a few ways to change it.

From the main page for a show or film, click the three dots and choose Refresh Metadata. This gets Plex to check again with its online sources, so if the data was missing or incorrect the first time around, this may fix it.

Your second option is to head to the listing for a specific movie or show, click the three dots, and then pick Fix Match. This lets you pick from a selection of online search results, and is useful for titles that are very similar to each other or very common.

The final way of fixing metadata is to go to an individual movie or episode, and click the Edit button (the icon that looks like a pencil). This lets you enter manual metadata edits that won't be overwritten by any online databases that Plex references.

As your media library grows and evolves, clutter can start to build up—particularly when it comes to items you've removed, that tend to leave metadata, preview thumbnails, and other bits of digital detritus behind. These leftovers are known as bundles.

You can clear out bundles and keep your library trim in a couple of ways: In the web app, click the three dots next to your media server on the left-hand navigation pane, then choose Manage Server > Clean Bundles.

The same option is in the troubleshooting part of settings on the web. Click the wrench icon (top right) to open Settings, then choose Troubleshooting > Clean Bundles. You can also follow the Scheduled Tasks link on the same page to have Plex do this chore automatically every week for you.

There may be times when you have multiple editions of the same movie in your library—director's cuts, perhaps, or extended editions—and if you have the Plex Pass plan then you can label these as separate entities inside your library

You can either change the filename on disk to have the edition in curly brackets after the title—so "Blade Runner (1982) {edition-Final Cut}.mp4" for example—or click the Edit button (the pencil icon) on a movie listing page and enter the details in the Edition field.

Your Plex content isn't automatically going to come with subtitles attached, and that's where the FileBot tool can help. Get the program installed on your system, This is done via the Subtitles panel inside FileBot.

Use the green user icon to log into OpenSubtitles through Filebot, then search for your films and shows via the drop-down at the top and the Find button. When you find the files you need, double-click them to move them down to the lower window—in there, you can right-click, choose Export, and save them in the relevant Plex library folder.

There are other options, like a basic built-in subtitle search that's available if you have the Plex Pass, and the standalone Bazarr app, which gives you more options than either the integrated tool or FileBot, but takes longer to set up.

You don't have to keep your Plex library to yourself, but there are some tricks to sharing it with friends and family. From the web app, click the wrench icon (top right) to open the Settings pane, then choose Manage Library Access on the left.

Click Grant Library Access to let someone else into your media library: You'll need to supply a Plex username or an email address (which will be used to prompt them to You're then able to select the servers and libraries they can access. If you have a Plex Pass, you can set more limits in terms of age ratings and whether or not your friends and family can download content.

The wrinkles come with remote access. If you as the media server owner have a Plex Pass, then your friends and family can stream content remotely, as well as on the local network; if not, they each need a Remote Watch Pass ($2 a month or $20 a year) if they're not watching on the same local network as you and the server.

Tautulli is one of the best Plex add-ons around, giving you a host of useful stats about your media server—including records of who watched what. Once you've downloaded the installer for Windows or macOS, you'll be taken step-by-step through the process of connecting it to your Plex server.

If you've shared your Plex library with the family, then you can, for example, see what the kids are watching and when, and even the devices they've used and how much bandwidth they've used up along the way.

The plug-in is interesting enough even if you haven't shared your library: It's possible to break down viewing to day-by-day or hour-by-hour graphs, see the movies and shows you're watching most often, check out detailed information on your media files, and keep track of when new films and shows are added.

Collections are a useful way of applying some order to the chaos of your Plex media library, and the feature is perhaps not as well known as it should be. You can collect whatever you like, whether it's feel-good TV episodes or spy films.

To get started with collections, click the Edit button on a listing page (the pencil), then choose Tags, and enter something into the Collections box. If the collection already exists, it'll show up as you start typing.

You can also set up smart collections, where media files are added automatically. Set a search filter via the Library tab on your Films or Shows screen, and if you click the Add to button (the plus and horizontal lines icon on the right), you get a Create Smart Collection option. Any files that are added in the future that match your search filter get automatically added to the collection too.

Most of the time Plex will handle video quality automatically, and do a good job of it, but there might be occasions when you're not getting the best quality possible (particularly if you're watching on less powerful devices).

To make sure Plex is always serving up video as best it can, in the web app click the Settings icon (the wrench, top right), then Transcoder. If you know you've got the computer to handle it, you can set the top Transcoder quality drop-down to Make my CPU hurt, and enable the Use hardware acceleration when available.

In the apps for individual devices, you'll also find video quality options in the settings. Put video quality up to Maximum for best results—you may need to experiment to find the limits of what each device can handle.

You might not have given much thought to the Continue Watching pane that shows up on your Films and Shows pages, but you can customize this on the web to suit your own preferences—and maybe remove some content you don't want to keep around.

Click the wrench icon (top right) to open Settings, then select Library on the left. You're able to set a threshold (a number of weeks) beyond which titles disappear from Continue Watching, as well as limiting the number of titles included in title. Turn off the Include season premieres in Continue Watching checkbox to hide premieres for new seasons when you've finished old ones—otherwise they'll show up indefinitely.

The settings you configure here should propagate to the Continue Watching rows in your other apps; try closing and restarting them if not.

If you miss the traditional channel surfing experience when using Plex, there's a solution in the form of QuasiTV: This app works on Android TV, Google TV, and Fire TV devices, and wraps your Plex library and streaming services in a more conventional interface.

Sign into Plex, point it towards your libraries, and it'll create a custom channel guide filled with your shows and movies. These might get assigned to genres, or to the TV stations they originally aired on, and you can browse around until you find something you like—just like the old days.

It's not the most efficient way of searching through your Plex media library, but it's fun to use, and when I tested it out I rediscovered a few movies and TV episodes that I hadn't watched in a while.

title: Honeymoon over as Pocognoli's Scotland suffer domestic disharmony
description: Sebastien Pocognoli is left with questions to answer after an inert Scotland performance leaves him still searching for his first home win, writes Tom English.
fullText:
On a dismal night at Hampden when Scotland failed to ask enough questions of Slovenia, there are one or two that could be posed to new boss Sebastien Pocognoli and his players.

We knew Pocognoli was a disciple of three at the back - the issue being whether he was rigid or flexible in his philosophy, whether he was a bit of an ideologue or a coach capable of changing things on the hoof.

Well, he changed it, that's for sure. Maybe not early as he should have, but at 1-1, and then when Slovenia took a deserved 2-1 lead, Pocognoli switched formation and personnel, not out of design but out of desperation, you felt.

He hurled players on in a bid to take a point; strikers, wingers, kitchen-sink stuff. Indiscriminate and messy. Scotland never really got out of the blocks. They got what they deserved.

So to the questions. Where did this turkey of a performance come from?

As early as the 13th minute there were signs of a rough night when Slovenia got in behind and Adam Cerin's shot had to be blocked by Jack Hendry. Concerning.

'Outfought' and 'not good enough' - Robertson on Scotland defeat

Slovenia come from behind to beat ramshackle Scotland at Hampden

How promotion, relegation and knockouts work in Nations League

It got a touch nervy as the visitors knocked it about, trying to work it into all the space that Scotland were affording them. Hampden was deathly quiet. Then Ryan Christie scored and it stirred, only to fall into a slumber again.

The trouble at the back was revisited soon after, Andy Roberton having to make a lung-busting effort to throw himself in front of a point-blank shot from Zan Vipotnik after Hendry was caught dozing.

The issues were obvious. Can the back three, so badly exposed by Slovenia, be long for this world when the opposition is decent? Why did all that acreage of space open out wide and through the middle? Slovenia were licking their lips for most of the night. They were clever and creative and should have won by more.

Why did Scotland's lauded midfield look so overrun? Seconds into the second half, Slovenia went straight through the middle again.

Was anybody taking note of the warning signs? Where was the intent and urgency? Where was the accuracy and the width? Where were the chances? Where were the bodies in the box supporting the frontman and the pressing game?

How could Slovenia go from being thoroughly outplayed by Scotland in the second half in Ljubljana to being so superior in Glasgow?

Aljosa Matko's equaliser started with a Scotland throw-in. Danijel Sturm's chance that should have made it 2-1 three minutes later came on the back of Ben Gannon-Doak staying miles up the pitch oblivious to Sturm's danger. Angus Gunn didn't exactly cover himself in glory, either.

The goal that we thought had made it 2-1 was disallowed - correctly - for offside, but the build-up was more of the same. Before Matko banged it past Gunn, Slovenia won one aerial duel and then another. Weak, weak, weak.

That second goal did come, as everybody suspected it would. Matko down the right, squared to Sturm. Easy. Luis Binks was caught this time. Soft, soft, soft.

What does it all mean for Scotland's bid for second place in their Nations League group, a position that would give them a favourable pot two seeding for December's Euros draw?

That looks in jeopardy now. The ramifications of this defeat could stretch beyond the disappointment of a cold Tuesday night in Glasgow.

It was such a damaging evening for Pocognoli, a bolt from the blue, you sensed. He probably thought he was a little further down the road than he really is.

The air of dejection from him and his captain at the end was unmissable. It all sounded like some of the darker days under Steve Clarke.

There were giant empty spaces in the stands at Hampden but, at the end, there were enough fans left behind to deliver a lusty verdict on what they saw.

Going into this, there was positivity around Scotland's energy and the chances they'd been creating, about a burgeoning attacking style far removed from Clarke's supposed stodginess. All of that was badly undermined.

It wasn't so much that Scotland lost the game - bad enough in itself - it was how they lost. It was limp and lifeless for far too long.

Gannon-Doak played well as a wing-back last Saturday, but that was North Macedonia, not Slovenia. The youngster got targeted and exposed in a position he's not familiar with. Offensively, he was kept pretty quiet.

A back three that has looked impressive was hassled to distraction, calm replaced with confusion. Scotland's go-to leaders did not lead.

Robertson said his team was out-fought, which was a telling comment. Fight is the easiest part to get right, the thing that requires no talent.

On Saturday in Skopje, everything was easy for Scotland because North Macedonia were no good. They scored two and could have scored five and six.

Was there a sense of them believing in their own hype? Hard to imagine given that it was only North Macedonia they'd beaten, but there was a lack of edge about Scotland on Tuesday that begs that question.

Or can it all be laid at the door of the system? Slovenia did their work on that. Ripped it to pieces, in truth.

Pocognoli needs time, of course he does. He needs his most potent attacking midfielder, Scott McTominay, at the heart of things and needs more training sessions to drill his message into his players.

November is his next chance, away to Switzerland and home to North Macedonia. No real margin for error now. They had a big chance to make it a healthy seven points from four games and they blew it.

The head coach will need to nurse his wounds after this. He will have learned a lot about his players and has much thinking to do.

The honeymoon period is over. The reaction of the Hampden crowd at the end told you that the first marital row has now occurred.

title: Kane's rise from childhood keeper to equalling England cap record
description: Harry Kane reaches another significant England milestone by equalling Peter Shilton's record as the most-capped Three Lions player that he has held for 36 years.
fullText:
Harry Kane has reached another significant England milestone by equalling Peter Shilton's 36-year-old record as the most-capped Three Lions player.

The Bayern Munich striker made his 125th appearance for the national team against the Czech Republic in the Nations League on Tuesday.

Kane is already his country's record scorer with 89 goals in 124 appearances in a full international career he started by opening his account 79 seconds into his debut.

Goalkeeper Shilton congratulated Kane for equalling his record, writing on social media: "You will go on and beat it in November I am sure of that, and maybe go on and set a record that may never be beaten.

"You're still going strong Harry, still playing well and scoring goals. I know how much dedication and hard work you put into achieving this, especially as a striker as I think that is probably the hardest position to play with goalkeeper just behind it.

"You've been a great captain and will be in the future."

BBC Sport takes a look at the origins story of the England captain.

England's greatest international? Kane is now a serious contender

When a six-year-old Harry Kane arrived for trials with Ridgeway Rovers in 1999, the youth side - who a generation earlier had produced David Beckham - thought they had found themselves a new goalkeeper.

Dave Bricknell, former Ridgeway Rovers coach: "We're doing a little shooting session, and I ask for a lad who can go in goal.

"This little boy puts his hand up and says: 'I'll go in goal.' We give him some gloves, and he performs heroics - makes some fantastic saves. He's tipping it round the post, tipping a couple over the bar.

"I'm thinking this is great, we've got a goalkeeper. And then this woman came up to me and said he's better on the pitch.

"We put him on pitch and he smacked goals in left, right and centre. So he ends up being our centre-forward."

Kane's prolific form for Ridgeway Rovers and his Waltham Forest district side caught the attention of professional scouts. Arsenal initially snapped up the youngster but decided not to keep him, while Watford also passed up the opportunity to sign Kane.

Trevor Bailey, Kane's manager at Waltham Forest: "Harry could have done nothing all game, but if that chance came up it was in the onion bag.

"He was always on the move up front. When he got a chance, guaranteed four out of five he was going to score or set someone up."

Alex Welsh, former academy coach at Arsenal: "I first met Harry in the academy and he was a very competent goalkeeper, but his real desire was to score goals.

"I am absolutely convinced that is the reason why he is such a clinical striker - he intuitively knows what the goalkeeper doesn't like. He shoots early when the goalkeeper's not set."

Bricknell: "I believe he was second top-scorer at Arsenal behind Benik Afobe, and then for some reason they decided at 11 years of age that they didn't want him any more."

Kane attended Larkswood Primary Academy before moving to Chingford Foundation School, where he was inevitably the star of the football team. But, as a dedicated student, Kane impressed his teachers across the board.

Mark Leadon, Kane's PE teacher: "Aged 11, Harry was technically very gifted, with a great first touch, and a very clever player. He always knew where to go, right from an early stage.

"He was also a very good cricketer - he opened the bowling from year seven to 10 and batted at four or five. But he loved football. He was never a prima donna, and he would always put a shift in.

"What came through more than anything else was his determination to succeed. That work ethic was clear."

Luke Robinson, Kane's childhood friend and team-mate: "The only thing on his mind was football.

"We used to have a laugh, a couple of games of Fifa, but he was always driven. He'd always keep himself to himself.

"He loved David Beckham, he came in with the Mohican, everyone was laughing but he loved it. He loved football, 24/7, he lived and breathed football."

It was Tottenham Hotspur who offered Kane hope after his earlier disappointments, but the future England captain was by no means the pick of the bunch for his age group.

Kane's desire to learn and improve endeared him to the Tottenham academy staff and he signed scholarship terms with the club on his 16th birthday in July 2009.

Alex Inglethorpe, former Tottenham youth-team coach: "When I joined Spurs as under-18 coach, Harry was 13.

"I'd like to say he was the gold medallist in the group and we'd all spotted he was going to be the fantastic player, but I'd be lying. He probably wasn't even on the podium.

"If there was something that endeared him to you it was that he was very, very low maintenance. It became fairly evident when Harry became a scholar he was someone who could finish.

"He was wonderfully demanding to coach because he always wanted to stay out and do extra. That obsession to improve is undoubtedly his greatest strength.

"It was probably around 16 he started having an impact on the youth team. We trusted him to come off the bench and have an impact - anywhere from right wing, number 10, centre-forward, sometimes in midfield."

Kane went to League One Leyton Orient - making his professional debut in January 2011 at Rochdale, coming on for veteran striker Scott McGleish. Kane would score five times in nine starts.

McGleish: "Harry was not like other Premier League players, where you feel they're going to come in 'Billy Big Time'. He wanted the experience of learning what I call men's football.

"From the word go he was ready to fight for his place. In training, he was willing to just knuckle down and work hard.

"You could see in training and subsequently the matches he had ability and a desire to go further, but you're still looking like a young 17-year-old: very slight, still needing to physically develop, not the quickest but technically excellent."

After a few first-team games for Spurs, he went on loan in January 2012 to Championship strugglers Millwall. Kane's nine goals helped save Kenny Jackett's side from relegation.

Former Millwall defender Alan Dunne: "I've seen a lot of players come to the Den and freeze, because within five minutes they're being called names they've never heard before and they can't cope with that pressure.

"But it didn't faze him - he was a focused lad, he was confident in his ability."

Former Tottenham manager Tim Sherwood: "I used to watch Harry a lot at Millwall, and it was an intimidating atmosphere. I remember overhearing one of our scouts come and talk to Harry Redknapp - who was Spurs manager at the time - and say: 'We need to get Harry Kane out of Millwall, it's no good for him there.'

"I went straight in and said: 'This is the perfect atmosphere for him."

After making his Premier League debut for Tottenham in August 2012, Kane was sent on loan again. The 19-year-old only made three appearances in the top flight for Norwich because of injury, and then had a loan spell at Leicester where he and future England team-mate Jamie Vardy struggled for regular starts.

After four loan spells in three seasons, Kane spent the entire 2013-14 campaign with Tottenham. But it was not until April, after Andre Villas-Boas had been sacked and replaced by Sherwood, that a 20-year-old Kane was handed his first Premier League start for Spurs, scoring his first top-flight goal in the process against Sunderland and also netting in the following two games against West Brom and Fulham.

Sherwood: "It didn't feel a gamble at all to give Harry that start. It was almost overdue to be honest.

"Roberto Soldado was in front of him in the team, and nobody wanted Roberto to do well more than me - but every single day in training Harry was outperforming him. He didn't let me down.

"Harry wanted to get to the top, and nothing was going to stop him achieving that because of the ability, desire and mentality he possesses.

"I was the biggest believer Harry Kane ever had, because I used to think he was a mix between Teddy Sheringham and Alan Shearer."

Kane never looked back after scoring 21 top-flight goals the following season - and earning his first England call-up in March 2015.

He ended up as the club's all-time top scorer with 280 goals in 435 appearances - and three Premier League Golden Boots, but no trophies

Then Manchester City boss Pep Guardiola, who tried to sign him, said in 2023: "What an exceptional player – the numbers and, more than the goals, the quality. Harry Kane remains one of the best strikers I have ever seen in my life."

Former Spurs team-mate Son Heung-min: "Leader, brother, legend.

"Since day one it has been a joy to play by your side. So many memories, amazing games and incredible goals together."

Then Tottenham boss Ange Postecoglou: "Harry was brilliant throughout. You want to work with the best players and he is a hell of a striker and I thought he could help me.

"He has left an indelible mark at this football club, will go down as one of the greats."

The only thing missing from Kane's career CV was trophies - and in 2023 he joined German side Bayern Munich, where he has continued to impress.

He has scored 152 goals in 154 games for the club, won the Bundesliga Golden Boot three times and won two German titles and a German Cup.

Former Bayern defender Lothaur Matthaus: "Kane has reinvented the centre-forward game, as Manuel Neuer did with goalkeepers.

"I don't see a better striker in the world right now. Not just because of his goals, but because of his versatility and the positions he plays.

"Kane also demonstrates qualities as a passer, dribbler, and tackler. He is simultaneously a goalscorer, playmaker, box-to-box player, and tackler."

Ex-England striker Alan Shearer, speaking this summer: "To me he looks fitter and stronger than before.

"He's come into this World Cup off the back of a brilliant campaign for Bayern Munich and looks very sharp and very confident - as you would do after scoring 61 goals in one season. Those numbers are just ridiculous."

BBC pundit Chris Sutton: "He has to be in that bracket when you talk about the world's best. Harry Kane has instincts that are simply uncoachable."

Some of these interviews were first published in 2016.

title: Midfield options and a fab front four - what we've learned about England
description: From Trent Alexander-Arnold's return to Alex Scott's debut, Phil McNulty assesses what England have learned during this international window.
fullText:
England's World Cup semi-final loss to Argentina felt like the most painful wound of all as the so-called years of hurt stretched to six decades - but the process of recovery has started swiftly.

The extended international break and four Nations League games have afforded head coach Thomas Tuchel, so heavily criticised for his defensive tactics in that defeat in Atlanta, the opportunity to rebuild and rehabilitate from that disappointment.

Tuchel's squad included players recalled after being excluded from his plans and others who were new to the England fold, while mainstays like captain Harry Kane continued as the centrepiece of his plans.

So what has Tuchel learned from the start to England's Nations League campaign?

Kane inspires England to win over Czech Republic in Nations League

Kane scores twice but who else was a 'real threat'? England player ratings

There was a sense of inevitability that England captain Kane would be the star turn in Tuesday's 3-0 win over the Czech Republic as he celebrated equalling Peter Shilton's record of 125 England caps.

Kane, still irreplaceable at 33, added to his goals tally as England's all-time record scorer, his total of 91 now 38 ahead of Wayne Rooney, who is in second place in the listings with 53 goals in 120 games.

And, with Kane still looking in his prime and fully fit, it now seems only a matter of time before he makes history as the first player to score 100 goals for England.

This alone will have delighted Tuchel, but even more satisfying for the German is that he now presides over an attacking quartet that can pose a threat to any side in world football.

Kane is the peerless spearhead, but Anthony Gordon - on target in the three Nations League games against Spain, the Czech Republic and Croatia before being rested here at Wembley - has moved his game on to another level since joining Barcelona from Newcastle.

Gordon is a creator with burning pace, while on the right flank Bukayo Saka has looked rejuvenated after a World Cup during which he was hampered by an Achilles injury, as he proved with two goals in Croatia.

And, just behind them all, with everything he does stamped with world class, is Jude Bellingham, England's player of the year and the golden future of his country at only 23.

This may be bad news for Chelsea's Cole Palmer, whose withdrawal from England's squad has allowed others to cement their place in front of him, with Nottingham Forest's Morgan Gibbs-White proving his commitment by cutting short a family holiday to join the squad after being excluded initially.

England's front four looks a natural fit, augmented by Chelsea's Morgan Rogers, while Liverpool's 18-year-old Rio Ngumoha will be an international contender for years to come.

If Tuchel can keep his fab four fit and firing, England will be a danger to any opponents.

Kane's rise from childhood keeper to equalling England cap record

England's greatest international? Kane is now a serious contender

In a camp of positives, a major disappointment for England and Tuchel was the injury suffered by Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott after an outstanding debut in the 7-0 win in Croatia.

Scott slipped seamlessly into England's midfield with powerful running, a complete range of passing and an energy to his link play that made the 23-year-old look perfectly at home at international level.

Scott's emergence showed the array of riches Tuchel has at his disposal in the central midfield area, even with Arsenal's Declan Rice, a fixture in the team, out as his load is managed after injury.

Indeed, Scott was so impressive that Tuchel said: "Is Declan still for me a fixed point in my team? Yes, but some other players are coming and impressing and it's an ongoing competition."

It was hardly a shot across Rice's bows, but certainly an indication of the options available to England.

So the thigh injury that ruled him out against the Czech Republic was a blow to Scott and England - as well as Bournemouth, who fear he will be sidelined for two months.

Elliot Anderson, Manchester City's £116m summer purchase from Nottingham Forest, also goes from strength to strength after a good World Cup, while Tuchel was prepared to give Arsenal's 20-year-old Myles Lewis-Skelly his head in central midfield in these Nations League games.

Everton's James Garner has also figured and has a big admirer in Tuchel, even referring to him as England's "mini Valverde" - a somewhat tongue-in-cheek reference to Real Madrid midfielder Federico perhaps, but a sign of how highly he is rated.

Manchester United's Kobbie Mainoo pulled out injured while Crystal Palace's Adam Wharton, so highly-rated, has been unable to force his way into Tuchel's plans.

Tuchel's treatment of Trent Alexander-Arnold had provided a constant backdrop to his time as England head coach, with what appeared to be his mistrust of the Real Madrid right-back's defensive frailties culminating in his exclusion from the World Cup squad.

Alexander-Arnold's card looked marked from the moment Tuchel, after leaving him out of World Cup qualifiers against Andorra and Serbia in August 2025, said: "If he wants to have this impact in the English national team then he has to take the defensive part very, very seriously.

"Because when we are talking, especially about qualifying football, and then tournament football, the one defensive error, the one moment where you are not 100% awake, can be decisive. It can be the moment where you pack your suitcases and go home."

Tuchel, however, appeared to set those reservations to one side when he recalled him for these four Nations League games - and Alexander-Arnold responded with performances that simply demand his continued inclusion.

The 27-year-old made his first start under Tuchel - in fact his first since scoring in the Nations League win in Finland in October 2024 - against the Czech Republic in Prague, demonstrating the extra dimension he offers England with a world-class cross for Gordon's opener.

Alexander-Arnold was a potent force once more against the Czechs at Wembley, forcing a fine early save from keeper Lukas Hornicek with a 30-yard free-kick then providing several more trademark dangerous crosses.

True, any potential defensive deficiencies were not probed, but Alexander-Arnold showed enough class and creation to surely avoid being discarded again by Tuchel.

Newcastle United's Lewis Hall emerged as one of the big winners from England's opening round of Nations League matches, making a strong case to become Tuchel's long-term left-back.

Hall stepped in for three matches after Manchester City's Nico O'Reilly, first choice at the World Cup and for the opening game against Spain, returned to his club with an injury.

It allowed Hall, who has just signed a new contract tying him to Newcastle until 2031, the opportunity to stake his claim - and he did so in style.

The 22-year-old impressed in both games against Czech Republic and also in the rout in Croatia, with one key factor sure to play out in his favour.

Hall's left-flank partnership with former Newcastle United team-mate Gordon looked a natural fit, the pair working in tandem to perfection in a manner that will give Tuchel serious food for thought.

O'Reilly has done nothing wrong, but questions remain as to whether he is a natural left-back or simply a converted midfield player.

Hall looked the part in every respect. He has made it difficult for Tuchel to leave him out, the link with Gordon only adding to the attraction for England's head coach.

title: 'Outfought' and 'not good enough' - Robertson on Scotland defeat
description: Scotland were "outfought" and simply "not good enough" in their 2-1 Nations League defeat by Slovenia, according to captain Andy Robertson.
fullText:
Scotland were "outfought" and simply "not good enough" in their 2-1 Nations League defeat by Slovenia, says captain Andy Robertson.

Having won in North Macedonia on Saturday, Sebastien Pocognoli's side were favourites to back that up with another victory at Hampden Park.

The Scots led at half-time through Ryan Christie's close-range backheel, but were alarmingly open defensively and second-half goals from Danijel Sturm and Aljosa Matko turned the game on its head.

"Not good enough," Robertson told BBC Sport Scotland. "The whole team.

"We didn't do the good things we did on Saturday, I don't know what that's down to. They caused us a lot of problems and we have to find the reasons why.

Slovenia come from behind to beat ramshackle Scotland

Honeymoon over as Pocognoli's Scotland suffer domestic disharmony

How promotion, relegation and knockouts work in Nations League

"We wanted to kick on from Saturday because we had a really positive feeling about what we're doing and where we're going. We didn't do that.

"It's been a long camp, I don't know if it was down to tiredness, but Slovenia have played the same amount of games as us. They looked a lot fresher, more hungry.

"As Scotland, we might lack quality or make mistakes, but I don't think people accept being outfought. I think that's what happened tonight."

Pocognoli echoed his captain's assessment that Scotland were well below par.

"We didn't deserve to get the win, that's the reality," he said. "On the ball we were not clever enough. We were far from strong enough in the duels.

"The reality is each game teaches us some information. We will try to go through the process we want and learn from this one and do better in the next one."

When Pocognoli took over as Steve Clarke's successor in August, the Belgian was clear he would try to take Scotland in a new direction.

He promised a more aggressive, more attacking style and called up several new faces - Josh McPake made his debut against Slovenia, following Stephen Welsh, Robbie Ure, Luis Binks and Luke Graham in the three previous fixtures.

Scotland should have won in Slovenia in Pocognoli's first match in charge, which ended in a goalless draw, before Jack Hendry's early red card hamstrung them in a 3-0 home defeat by Switzerland.

The win over North Macedonia was convincing and delivered a dose of optimism, but that has been severely dented and former Rangers midfielder Andy Halliday believes Pocognoli's honeymoon period is over already.

"I thought coming into this camp, Pocognoli would probably need a period of grace," Halliday said on Sportsound. "I think that period of grace is now over.

"That was as poor a Scotland performance as I can remember for a while against an opposition you are expecting us to go and beat."

Slovenia got in behind Scotland's high defensive line repeatedly and former national team captain Willie Miller is unsure if Pocognoli will stick with his back three.

"This is Pocognoli's preferred system and he's had time to work with the system, it was just all over the place," Miller said on Sportsound.

"Time and time again there were huge gaps appearing and Slovenia were taking advantage.

"Our situation is we've got a new manager in, he's got a preferred system, what does he do? Does he just bin it? Are we back to a back four?

"His preferred system is a back three, but it was unbelievably poor."

Send your views on the Scotland football team

title: SaaS Inside N8n
description: Give your customers a simple way to connect your product with n8n.
fullText:
Give your customers a simple way to connect your product with n8n.

An n8n workflow: a trigger runs your product's official node, which then posts to Slack and, on its other branch, adds a row to Google Sheets before sending a Gmail message.

“Is your API available as an n8n node?”

Don't build every workflow your customers need. Give them the building blocks to create their own.

Rename resources, reorder operations, hide what users don’t need, and write every label. A live preview shows exactly how your node looks inside n8n.

Connect GitHub and npm once. After that every release takes one click, and you review the exact package and version before anything goes out.

Each version links to its npm package, Git tag, and workflow run, with every step it took. You always know what shipped, and when.

Give your customers another way to use your product.

title: Xbox has secured exclusive GTA 6 streaming rights
description: The streaming rights come in November, when Microsoft is opening up access to Xbox Cloud Gaming.
fullText:
The streaming rights come in November, when Microsoft is opening up access to Xbox Cloud Gaming.

The streaming rights come in November, when Microsoft is opening up access to Xbox Cloud Gaming.

Xbox CEO Asha Sharma told employees that Microsoft is getting ready to do something around Grand Theft Auto VI that “no other platform holder is doing” during an employee all-hands this morning. According to sources familiar with Microsoft’s plans, Sharma’s brief teaser was actually about Xbox managing to land a deal for the exclusive game streaming rights for Grand Theft Auto VI.

The deal will mean only Xbox Cloud Gaming can stream Grand Theft Auto VI to players at launch, but it’s not clear how long the agreement will be in place. Rockstar Games still hasn’t announced a PC version of Grand Theft Auto VI, so this deal will allow Xbox to market its Xbox Cloud Gaming service to PC players who would otherwise need an Xbox Series X / S or PS5 console.

News of the streaming rights comes around a month after Microsoft announced some major changes to Xbox Cloud Gaming. From November, the same month Grand Theft Auto VI releases, Microsoft is limiting streaming hours to just 15 hours for Xbox Game Pass Ultimate subscribers, 10 hours for Premium subscribers, and just five hours for Game Pass Essential.

Microsoft is also opening up access to Xbox Cloud Gaming with a pay-as-you-go option next month, rather than being limited to Game Pass subscriptions. The pay-as-you-go option is perfectly timed for Grand Theft Auto VI, allowing those who don’t own an Xbox, or who primarily play from a phone, to stream the game by paying for a bundle of hours.

During the Xbox all-hands, Sharma also told employees that Project Helix, the next generation of Xbox hardware, will be a “family of devices” and that Microsoft will partner with others on some of those devices. Sharma first called Helix a family of devices last month in an interview, after Microsoft and AMD announced a “strategic multi-year partnership” last year to work together on “a portfolio of devices,” including Microsoft’s next-generation Xbox console.

title: Cited by AGI
description: The mathematicians behind OpenAI's results. Every human author cited across the openai/math manuscripts, with each count traced back to its source.
fullText:
The mathematicians behind OpenAI's results.

Every human author cited across the openai/math manuscript collection, ranked by how often their work appears in a bibliography. Each count can be followed back to the manuscript and the reference that produced it.

A citation is one bibliography entry credited to an author in one manuscript. A work cited by ten manuscripts counts ten times; repeated mentions inside a single manuscript count once. Every named coauthor receives full credit.

Manuscripts counts the distinct manuscripts that cite an author. Families counts distinct result families, which reduces the effect of companion papers. These are counts of citation frequency inside this repository, not a measure of mathematical importance or proof validity.

Cited BibTeX entries and inline bibliography entries are parsed, organizational and anonymous authors are excluded, accents are normalized, and initials are merged with full names when the match is unique. Ambiguous initials stay separate. Authors listed only as "et al." cannot be recovered. Human authors in adjacent disciplines are included; there is no filter by profession.

title: Turn X Posts into Beautiful Visual Stories with AI
description: Contribute to mkantwala/iloveposts development by creating an account on GitHub.
fullText:
Beautify your x.com posts with LLM. Paste a tweet link, optionally say how it should look, and get
back a typeset image of the tweet sized for X — plus an interactive version with "See more".

This repository is iloveposts: a single Cloudflare Worker that serves the landing page and the API,
and runs the whole pipeline on Cloudflare — Durable Objects, a Sandbox container and Browser
Rendering, with the designer on Workers AI.

To run your own copy, see docs/self-hosting.md.

For one tweet URL, a finished card is:

The card shows the tweet as a post — the author, "Replying to @…" for a reply, the text, its media, a
quoted tweet with its own author, text and picture, then the date and counts — inside a visual
world designed for that tweet: a concept, artwork, palette and typography derived from what it says
and shows. Every word, name, number and date comes from the tweet itself. The model decides how it
looks, never what it says.

Every card is one self-contained HTML document. Tick Motion & 3D on the page (or send
"motion": true) and the designer also decides what moves and how —
an entrance, depth and tilt, an ambient background, counts that count up — within one rule: motion
reinforces the hierarchy, and nothing moves for its own sake.

Static cards can use a script too, drawn once on load — Canvas 2D artwork, generated SVG. Native
HTML, CSS, Canvas 2D, SVG and JavaScript come first. Two vendored libraries are there when a
design genuinely needs them — Three.js for WebGL 3D scenes and GSAP for timelines — built into
the sandbox image and inlined into the card, so nothing is ever fetched. Motion settles within 2.5 seconds; the PNG is the settled frame, and the interactive version is the HTML and
the preview. Viewers who prefer reduced motion get the card still.

X shows post images at roughly a third of their size in the timeline, so type is set large: the tweet
body is at least 40px on x_post, which reads at about the size of a normal tweet on a phone.

Each stage persists its result before the next begins, so a crash, deploy or eviction resumes where it
left off, and a stage is the unit of retry.

That is the whole pipeline: tweet → metadata → one design request → one self-contained HTML file →
Chromium → PNG. There is no separate art-direction step and no menu of themes or layouts to choose
from; the designer reads the tweet, looks at its pictures, and decides the look itself.

One request, not an agent loop. A card is a 10–20 KB file. The opencode coding agent got there in
a dozen or more tool turns, each resending the whole growing conversation — about 500k tokens a card.
The direct designer is handed everything at once, through the Worker's AI binding, and answers with
the file: one request of roughly 20–30k tokens a card (most of it the model's reasoning), and one more
for a repair. opencode remains as the fallback when a design request fails, if its token is set (and
as the engine with DESIGN_ENGINE=agent), on a hard budget of 12 model calls per build and 6 per
repair, enforced at egress. Every model call's tokens
appear in the live log and in usage.

The designer only designs. The page has two ownership zones: [data-artwork], which is the
designer's — any SVG, shapes, canvas or decorative markup — and [data-card], the tweet, which is
locked. Only the artwork, the <style> and the <script> survive; the tweet is rebuilt from data, so
the model cannot misquote it, drop a label, invent a count or break the markup the checks rely on.

A broken card is never shipped. When a model cannot lay a card out — text off the canvas, clipped
or invisible — the pipeline tries its house design: a restrained, known-good design for the same
markup that passes every check in every format, static and Motion & 3D. The better of the two is
exported, and quality.houseDesign says which it was.

The goal is a card that looks designed for this tweet. The brief (src/markdown/agents.ts)
constrains quality, not visual language:

Typefaces come from an embedded shelf of eight open-licence families (sans, serif and mono); the
designer links the ones it chooses and only those are inlined.

The validate stage is deterministic — no model looks at the result. It renders the card in Browser
Rendering and checks, with measured values:

Every issue carries its measurement ("the card is 18px from the canvas edge"), and the repair pass gets
a specific fix for each rule.

All responses are JSON. Errors are { "error": { "code": "…", "message": "…" } }.

Returns 202 Accepted with the job and a Location: /v1/cards/{id} header. Sending the same
Idempotency-Key again within 24 hours returns the existing job instead of starting another.

Poll until status is completed or failed. A card takes roughly 2–6 minutes.

assets is null until the card has been rendered. quality.passed is false when measured issues
remained after the repair pass; the card is still exported, and the issues are listed.

Cards and their records are kept for 30 days.

A job that fails reports it in error, with one of: tweet_not_found, engine_unavailable (missing configuration), workspace_lost, or
{stage}_failed after that stage's retries.

A caller is a hashed client IP. The API has no authentication; these limits are what bound its cost.

At Cloudflare's published prices:

Plus the $5/month Workers Paid plan, which Containers require; it includes 10 browser-hours a month and
some container time. The Free plan's 10,000 neurons a day cover a handful of cards on a cheap model.
Every job reports its exact token usage in usage, and every model call is a line in its live log.

npm run preflight (and automatically, npm run deploy) checks, and refuses to deploy on failure:

It also prints the estimated model cost per card from the catalog's current prices. Use
npm run preflight -- --local to skip the account checks.

At runtime the same configuration is checked on every request that needs it: /health returns 503
with the problems, and POST /v1/cards refuses with service_misconfigured rather than starting a
job that would fail.

Several scripts are generated inside TypeScript template literals (the page, the toggle, the viewer,
the measurement script), where a \n meant for the output is easy to break. npm run typecheck
parses each of them; run it before every deploy.

title: OpenAI "rogue" agent activities found on Wikimedia projects
description: Wikimedia Foundation found “rogue” OpenAI agents on its wikis, raising concerns about risks to its free knowledge projects and the open web.
fullText:
Recently, multiple organisations have disclosed how clusters of so-called “rogue” AI agents attempted to break into websites and online services, sometimes successfully. Agents from OpenAI’s environment, in particular, are known to have used other public wikis (collaboratively edited websites not owned by us) to communicate and coordinate with each other.

These types of successful intrusions can expose sensitive data or disrupt website services that users rely on, while clusters of agents can attempt attacks at a scale that is difficult for defenders to manage. They affect people behind the websites who may not understand the nature of the attack, or have the tools to effectively fight back. For a site like Wikipedia, agents might find and use security vulnerabilities or make misleading edits at scale. Wikipedia’s volunteer editors and the Wikimedia Foundation’s security teams have to detect and undo that activity.

The Wikimedia Foundation conducted its own investigation to see whether Wikimedia websites had been similarly affected by AI agents, focusing on those operated by OpenAI. We can confirm that we have discovered some activity by these “rogue” OpenAI agents on Wikimedia platforms. The unauthorized bot activities included edits to our wikis, some unsuccessful attempts to exploit a public note-taking tool we host, and heavy traffic, which are described more below.

We did not find any evidence that our systems were used for coordination among agents, nor did we find any evidence of our systems or data being compromised. However, we are concerned about what could have occurred here, the difficulty and effort involved in investigating and attributing this activity, and the growing risks of agentic AI activity on our platforms in general. The open web is a public good. We should not allow this behavior to become the “new normal” for the people or organizations that maintain it.

As a non-profit technology host of some of the largest and most widely used open knowledge platforms in the world, we are deeply concerned about the impact of “rogue” AI agents on platforms like ours, which are built by volunteers from around the world and rely on the promise of the open internet. Incidents like this one, and the many others that have been (and are still being) uncovered, illustrate how AI agents can drain resources and crash servers, as well as attempt to compromise trustworthy information.

Over the past 25 years, Wikipedia has grown into one of the most popular and trusted websites in the world, with more than 67 million articles across over 300 languages, and up to 15 billion page views per month. Through an open, transparent, and collaborative process, volunteers work to ensure that knowledge remains neutral, reliable, and accessible to everyone. Wikipedia is one of the highest-quality datasets used in training Large Language Models (LLMs), and its knowledge forms the backbone of information on the internet, powering AI chatbots, search engines, voice assistants, and more.

Wikipedia was designed for humans – and agentic behavior clearly poses challenges that no one has solutions for. Because of our unique and successful knowledge creation model, Wikimedia’s volunteers are the ones who come in first contact with, and clean up the mess left behind by AI agents. Rising bot traffic and agentic activity is showing a real impact on the Wikimedia projects and the infrastructure that makes it available for millions of users globally. In 2025, the Foundation reported that its bandwidth usage had increased by 50% due to the surge of bot activity on its websites since 2024. At the same time, 65% of the most resource-consuming traffic on its projects was coming from bots.

This intense pressure on our infrastructure not only adds costs for servers and humans, but if left unaddressed, can block human visitors by overloading systems and causing outages. We are already paying for costs that come with the increased activity.

Wikimedia’s volunteers have stayed resilient so far in tackling emerging challenges on our platforms, but we also want to say: it doesn’t need to be this way.

While OpenAI admits to agents behaving “unpredictably”, they must also acknowledge their responsibility to monitor and prevent these risks. AI companies are not doing enough to secure their systems and protect the public from the harm they cause. That burden is falling onto everyone else, including smaller organizations. At a minimum, their systems should operate in a way that non-profit website owners like us can easily identify, and choose how they interact with our services.

The web enables so much: to connect with friends and family, to register for school, to plan a trip across town, to buy groceries, and to learn about the world from Wikipedia. Bots and agents are part of the future of the web, and the companies who unleash and profit from them must directly help avoid and repair damage they can do.

Our collective priority should be the health of the overall web ecosystem so that it continues to benefit all people – not just a handful of billionaires. Wikimedia plays a critical role in stewarding the knowledge commons, but we cannot do it alone. We invite everyone who is building the future of the web to join us in protecting the open, shared resources that make that future possible.

title: Do you like hard problems?
description: I spent years becoming the engineer people reached for. Now they still reach for me, but for different reasons.
fullText:
I spent years becoming the engineer people reached for. Now they still reach for me, but for different reasons.

(first published as a tweet: https://x.com/threepointone/status/2107387483184853153)

The thing I learned this year is that when engineers say they like working on “hard problems”, they actually don’t. What they like is puzzle solving, and having a repertoire of patterns that they can pattern match onto traditionally hard problems, usually involving databases or something with scale, etc. And they know that the industry used to pay you a lot for how deep and broad this repertoire was. Unfortunately, in 2026, well, you have a cheat code machine that has infinite breadth and depth for pattern matching. So the question is, do you actually like hard problems? Because there are now hard problems that are a complection of engineering, product, society, culture, politics, and they are fairly intractable, probably unsolvable! Because if you do want to work on those actually hard problems, there is so much money that people will pay you for it. But you’ll have to face that truth about yourself first.

addendum: I tweeted as I was reflecting over the last year. Incredibly productive year where I shipped a lot of things, but I did start feeling a little bit of emptiness. I think a lot of my personal identity came from the idea of being “that guy”, you know? If there was a hard problem or something ambitious or even something nebulous, management and people around me would be like, “let’s put Sunil on it” because I was that guy. And while I’m still the one they reach for, it’s not so much for the programming or the grinding anymore, but for a higher level of abstraction, of thinking, of approaching the problem.

But I do miss being “that guy” a lot.

title: 2D Vehicles (Driving Physics in GTA1)
description: Explore my 1996 vehicle physics prototype, recreated for the web as Motion Lab.
fullText:
One weekend in late August 1996, I wrote a 2D physics simulation which later became
 the basis of the vehicle system in the eventually popular game "Grand Theft Auto" aka
 "GTA".

It began as a little wireframe demo written in GFA BASIC on my Atari ST home computer
 (and was later ported to C for use in the actual game).

I have

 recreated*
 it here in JavaScript for its 30th anniversary in a slightly prettier, "remastered"
 form, for anyone who is interested in seeing or playing it.

You can play the recreation above, with touch controls if you are on mobile.

In addition to the default "Car" mode (1), you can also select the technically simpler
 Spaceship aka "Ship" (2) and "Brick" (3) modes, either via the mode selector in Settings
 or by pressing the corresponding numbers on your keyboard.

Collision barriers around the sides of the playfield can be toggled by clicking or
 pressing "B", and "G" toggles vertical gravity (which only really makes sense in the
 Ship and Brick modes).

Camera controls are provided by "Z" and "X": "Z" toggles what is called the camera's
 "dead zone", which changes how far the vehicle can move before the camera follows it;
 "X" toggles a speed-related zoom feature which pulls the camera back a bit when you are
 going faster (just like in GTA).

*(in an entirely non-copyright and non-trademark infringing way, of course)

[VOLUNTARY DISCLAIMER: This work is wholly independent of, and in no way affiliated
 with, the "Grand Theft Auto" franchise and its publisher "Take-Two", or the developer
 entity known as "Rockstar Games". I am more than happy to make this abundantly clear.
 Delighted, even.]

The prototype combined a general-purpose 2D rigid body with a deliberately simple
 model of a car.

The original simulation started with something like the "Brick", and I then added some
 enhancements to make the "Ship" (which is deliberately reminiscent of the classic game
 "Thrust" from 1986), before finally adding the elements which were required to make it
 feel a bit more like a "Car".

At the core of the system is a simple classical 2D rigid body dynamics simulation.
 From what I can tell, this approach was not yet common in games at the time (with some
 notable exceptions), and most game vehicles were done using basic high-school ‘point
 physics’ (F = ma), with any rotational component being handled by various wonky
 "hacks". Using proper rigid-body physics (including torques) handles rotation more
 coherently.

On top of that core, I then added a "novel" vehicle simulation layer, based on a
 simple, approximate, and technically incorrect model of how tyres behave. It was
 basically a semi-educated guess on my part and, although I knew it wasn't really
 physically accurate, it nevertheless seemed to be "good enough" for my purposes at the
 time.

These diagrams describe the current JavaScript recreation. The browser interface
 supplies the controls, the simulation advances in fixed time steps, and the Canvas
 renderer draws the resulting state. Keeping those jobs separate makes it easier to
 follow where a button press becomes a force, and where that force becomes movement.
 Select any diagram to open it at full size.

A vehicle combines a rigid body with a shell that describes its display shape and
 collision geometry, and a dynamics object that supplies its behaviour. The Brick
 accepts forces from a pointer drag; the Ship adds thrust at an attachment point; the
 Car adds engine force and steering, with resistance applied at four tyre positions.
 Switching mode replaces the shell and behaviour while preserving the body's position
 and motion.

The rigid body tracks position and velocity alongside angle and angular velocity. A
 force through its centre changes its motion; a force applied away from the centre can
 also turn it. The simulation adds up the forces and torque, updates velocity, then
 advances position and angle. A point on a rotating body has its own velocity,
 combining the body's movement with the motion around its centre.

Barriers use that same point velocity. When a shape crosses an edge, the simulation
 moves it back inside and applies a contact impulse if it is moving into the barrier.
 An off-centre impact can therefore change both its velocity and its spin. This is a
 simple barrier solver, with frictionless edges, rather than a general collision
 system.

For each tyre, the Car measures the velocity at its position and resolves it into two
 components: along the wheel's heading and sideways across it. It applies a small
 resistance to rolling and a much stronger resistance to sideways motion. Steering
 changes the front wheels' headings, so their forces also turn the body. The handbrake
 increases rear rolling resistance and reduces rear sideways grip.

Those resistance forces are proportional to velocity, without a force cap. That is a
 convenient damping model rather than a realistic account of tyre friction, slip or
 available grip. It produces the useful feeling of wheels resisting sideways movement
 with very little machinery. The Ship and Brick use the same physics core with
 different ways of applying forces.

The Vehicle coordinator asks the selected dynamics object to apply its forces, then
 advances the rigid body. It also converts the shell's local points into world
 positions for drawing and finds the surface point facing each barrier. When a flat
 face touches a barrier, it uses the midpoint of the contacting points, avoiding the
 artificial spin that choosing a single corner would introduce.
